description: Counts here describe encoded TextUnit nodes, not the size or importance of original sources. Low counts can indicate incomplete extraction or graph modeling. Consult the cited source or review record before interpreting a gap.

doc:fl-science-2026-draft.note: The graph contains all 1,512 unique leaf benchmark IDs plus one non-leaf summary/range row; foreword and tables are separately cited in the corpus inventory.

doc:fl-science-2008.note: All 498 unique 2008 benchmark IDs are represented with full text, grade/code, and source locators. The graph also contains one composite legacy crosswalk row assigned to this source by the base graph; use the source-item total (498), not raw TextUnit count (499), as the 2008 benchmark denominator. The 1,494 semantic-neighbor links are machine-ranked leads only.

doc:fl-science-1996.note: The graph contains 170 TextUnits derived from the reviewed 1996 source-first set and crosswalk decompositions. The source-first review enumerates 56 original standards; 170 is not a count of original standards or a 2026 coverage denominator.

doc:fl-science-gle-1999.note: The graph contains 141 TextUnits representing 140 unique GLE codes plus one grade-placement record. This does not represent all historical revision artifacts.

doc:ngss-all-topic-standards.note: All 208 NGSS Performance Expectations are represented with text and PDF/extract locators. DCI descriptions, clarification statements, assessment boundaries, Appendix E progressions, MS-LS evidence statements, and NRC framework materials remain in the corpus but are not all itemized as graph nodes. The 624 semantic-neighbor links are machine-ranked leads only.

doc:external:8f3e333f4967c18a.note: Ten complete grade-level blocks (K–8 and 9–12) are encoded from the 2007 Florida Citizens for Science proposal. The source does not use item codes in this layout; no benchmark-level draft relation is inferred. Its front matter states that FCS claims no copyright interest.

doc:south-carolina-science-2014.note: Only the selected statements used in the external-source comparison are represented.

doc:external:89574ee13dd2c447.note: This record points to the same South Carolina source file as the named South Carolina source node. It is a data-model duplicate, not another independent source.

doc:external:9aab810f0e14c6e9.note: Only statements relevant to the bounded external comparison are represented.

doc:unassigned-source.coverage: 157 derived TextUnits lack a single sourceDocument
doc:unassigned-source.note: These are chiefly composite legacy crosswalk nodes that cite multiple historical source files in their sourceFiles field. They remain visibly unassigned because no single source edition accurately describes the whole composite. This is a data-modeling limitation, not a claim that their source material is unknown.

doc:external:indiana-2000.coverage: complete K–8 item extraction; human comparison incomplete
doc:external:indiana-2000.note: All 412 science statements from the nine ERIC-preserved grade booklets are represented. Three machine-ranked candidate links per item are discovery leads only; human omission review remains incomplete. The 1,236 candidate edges do not establish borrowing or omission.

corpusInventory.note: Inventory describes the local research corpus as of the graph build. It includes source documents, extracted text, research notes, and generated artifacts; counts do not imply every file is represented as a benchmark-level TextUnit. Copyright-sensitive external sources are linked or cited rather than reproduced wholesale.
